target: per-partition Hecke character chi^lambda(beta_atomic(Z,N); q_0) in the AVERAGED (colour-weighted) crossing convention
target_value: chi^lambda(beta; q) = tr rho^lambda_Hoefsmit(beta) with each crossing carried as a colour-weighted pair (c, d) rather than a bare sign; evaluated at the substrate anchor q_0
description:
Derivation chain for the per-lambda Hecke character caches at q_0 in the AVERAGED (colour-weighted) crossing convention -- the other of the corpus's two chi conventions, companion to chi-at-q0-sign-only-atomic.derivation.json. Covers eight nuclides: proton, neutron, deuteron, dineutron, diproton, tritium, helium-3, helium-4. Trust profile: one AXIOM entrypoint (the per-crossing Hecke energy), one MATHLIB_CITED step (Hoefsmit seminormal reps), three DERIVED steps, one SCRIPT_CITED frontier. Symbolic chain -- the target is the character identity, not a single number.

SCOPE. This is the averaged convention ONLY. The canonical convention corpus-side is sign-only (chi-convention-audit.witness.json, canonical_reconciliation; docs/audits/2026-06-09-binding-trace-convention-split.md), so these caches are the OFF-CANONICAL member of the split and are consumed by the binding-trace path, not by the Jones-Markov path. They are a different object from the sign-only caches, not a lower-precision version of them -- the deuteron differs by a factor of ~7 on lambda=(6).

OPEN, recorded rather than smoothed: a SECOND producer, compute_atom_chi_rust.py, emits four witnesses in this same convention (atom-chi-rust-{d,t,3he,4he}) and does NOT agree with this family. See step 6.

steps.name: Hecke relation and the balanced q-integer
steps.operation: The Iwahori-Hecke algebra H_n(q) is the braid-group algebra of B_n modulo (sigma_i - q)(sigma_i + q^{-1}) = 0. The eigenvalues q and -q^{-1} are the symmetric and antisymmetric crossing channels; their separation (q - q^{-1}) is the per-crossing Hecke energy scale, the AXIOM entrypoint of every Hecke-side chain.

steps.name: Hoefsmit seminormal representation rho^lambda of H_n(q)
steps.operation: Wedderburn-decompose H_n(q) over the partitions lambda |- n and realise each block by the Hoefsmit seminormal form: an explicit dim V_lambda x dim V_lambda matrix per generator, entries rational in q, determined by the axial distances of the standard Young tableaux. Semisimplicity holds because q_0 is not a root of unity.
steps.output_value: rho^lambda : H_n(q) -> End(V_lambda),  one block per lambda |- n
steps.notes: Identical to step 2 of the sign-only chain -- the representation is shared. The two conventions diverge only at the next step, in how a crossing of the braid word is turned into an element of H_n(q).

steps.name: Colour-weighted crossing: the (c, d) pair replaces the bare sign
steps.operation: Read each crossing of the canonical nucleus braid word on n = 3A strands as a PAIR (c, d) rather than a sign, and map it to the algebra element c*sigma_g + d*1. A same-colour crossing carries d = 0 and reduces to the sign-only case; the proton-neutron interface crossings carry d != 0, weighting the crossing by per-colour factors. Because the map is linear in the generator, the colour weighting expands by linearity through the representation.
steps.notes: This step IS the convention. Setting every d_j = 0 recovers the sign-only convention of chi-at-q0-sign-only-atomic.derivation.json; the two chains share steps 1-2 and diverge here. The corpus canon is sign-only (bean b0vf); this family is the other member of the split, retained because the binding-trace path consumes it.

steps.name: Block character chi^lambda(beta) := tr rho^lambda(beta)
steps.operation: Define the per-block character as the matrix trace of the represented braid word. Cyclicity makes it a class function on the braid, hence a function of the conjugacy class rather than of the chosen word.

steps.name: The one-row closed form does NOT survive colour weighting
steps.operation: On lambda = (n) every generator acts by the scalar q, so a sign-only word gives chi^(n) = q^{writhe}. Under colour weighting the one-row block instead evaluates prod_j (c_j q + d_j), which is not a power of q whenever any d_j is nonzero. This is the sharpest available test that a given cache is in this convention rather than the sign-only one.
steps.output_value: chi^(n)(beta; q) = prod_j (c_j q + d_j),  NOT q^{w}
steps.notes: Measured on the deuteron: this family gives chi^(6) = 1.5598701995641515927061, while the sign-only cache gives 11.021374980910484719107 = q_0^23 exactly (23 = the crossing count recorded in atomic-braid-recipe-d.derivation.json). A factor of ~7 apart -- the two conventions are different objects, not different precisions of one object. Scope-(a): this distinguishes the conventions, it does not rank them.

steps.name: Numerical evaluation at q_0 -- and a second producer that disagrees
steps.operation: Evaluate chi^lambda(beta_atomic(Z,N); q) at the substrate anchor for every lambda |- 3A, via the Hoefsmit mpfr path at 50 dps, for proton, neutron, deuteron, dineutron, diproton, tritium, helium-3 and helium-4.
steps.output_value: chi-{atom}-h{n}-at-q0-50dps caches for p, n, D, nn, pp, T, 3He, 4He
steps.notes:
script: computations/chi_at_q0_via_hoefsmit_mpfr.py -- the frontier step. Anchor: these witnesses declare q_0 inline at 50 dps and are PROTON-pinned (1.1099785827513808075916690956107688798744991218736).

OPEN DISCREPANCY, recorded not smoothed. computations/compute_atom_chi_rust.py emits four witnesses in this same convention (atom-chi-rust-{d,t,3he,4he}) and does NOT reproduce these values. Measured on the deuteron, per-partition relative difference ranges 6.96e-8 to 7.99e-7 -- eleven orders of magnitude above the 50-dps floor both claim. It is NOT the mu-p pin tension (1.15e-8, and both producers take the proton pin: chi_at_q0_via_hoefsmit_mpfr declares it inline, compute_atom_chi_rust imports q_parameter.Q) and NOT float64 q_0 truncation (~2e-16 after the ~23-crossing amplification). The two one-dimensional blocks, lambda = (6) and lambda = (1^6), disagree by exactly the same 6.956e-8 while higher-dimensional blocks disagree by up to 11x more, which points at the matrix products rather than at a scalar shift in q. Cause not established. Until it is, this chain covers the Hoefsmit family ONLY; the four compute_atom_chi_rust witnesses are deliberately NOT claimed by it. Also note those four record no q_0 at all, contrary to the AGENTS.md rule that a witness must say which pin it used.
